text:
devon: Heads-up — after the CUDA 12 rollout to eu-west reserved pool last night we've started seeing intermittent segfaults in the runtime on a subset of hosts. First noticed by a k8s OOM/killed pod, then an app SIGSEGV.

sanjay: Got a couple of core dumps. Patterns point to mismatch between the container-built libstdc++ and the host driver stack. stack traces show crashes in nvrtc and some kernel symbol lookups.

maria: Which nodes? any pattern by GPU model/driver?

devon: Affected nodes are nvidia-a100-rt-* (driver 535.x on host). Not all of them, roughly 6/48 in eu-west. Non-eu regions look fine.

ryan: Did the container rebuild use a different GCC/toolkit than previous images? Last week we rebuilt images with host's GCC 13 for C++17 compatibility. CUDA 12 toolkits were built against newer libstdc++. If host drivers expect symbols from older ABI, that can cause trouble.

devon: Build system log shows: `base: ubuntu-22.04, gcc: 13.1, cuda-toolkit: 12.1`. Previous stable used `gcc: 9` and `cuda-toolkit: 11.8`.

sanjay: Repro steps I ran locally: run container with `--gpus all`, execute a quick JIT compile call (torch.cuda.synchronize + torch.jit.trace) and it crashed after a few iterations. ldd on the offending .so shows mixed libstdc++ versions. snippet:

```
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6 => /usr/local/lib/libstdc++.so.6 (0x7f...)
/usr/local/cuda-12/lib64/libcudart.so => /usr/local/cuda-12/lib64/libcudart.so (0x7f...)
```

maria: :eyes: Are we shipping any local /usr/local/lib overrides in images? That would explain differing load order.

devon: Yes, the new build bakes a prebuilt third_party dir that includes its own libstdc++ to satisfy some old wheels. I missed that in the container diff.

infra-bot: deploys: rollback triggered — 1799876500 by devops. Rolling eu-west pool to last known-good image: r:2026-03-15_11:02.

alex: Good call to rollback. We need a plan: minimize flapping, ensure canary coverage, and produce a rebuild checklist.

ryan: Proposed immediate mitigation: pin container builds for CUDA 12 images to GCC 11 (libstdc++ ABI compatibility) or remove embedded libstdc++ and rely on distro lib. Also ensure NVIDIA container toolkit libs are not shadowed.

sanjay: I'll run a quick smoke matrix: (gcc {9,11,13}) x (cuda {11.8,12.1}) x (driver 525,535) on a dev host. Expecting the gcc13+cuda12 combo to fail when embedded libs are present.

maria: Cost/regression note — eu-west Dedicated capacity lost ~2 nodes for 3 hours while we triaged, caused query queueing and a handful of customer rate-limit escalations. Finance asked for an incident cost estimate.

devon: We'll capture cloud hours used and any burst instances invoked. Also track any failed jobs that retried.

alex: For the longer term: (1) add pre-deploy compatibility test that runs a minimal JIT kernel + NCCL ring test in a canary host; (2) update build pipeline to emit a "compat manifest" listing linked runtimes; (3) document recommended GCC range for CUDA 12 images in our infra README.

ryan: Also consider building a small shim that ldd-checks libs at container start and fails fast with an explicit error (and metric). That will avoid a silent segfault in production.

devon: Agree. I'll open a PR to: remove embedded libstdc++ from third_party, add the ldd preflight check, and pin the next canary to gcc11.

sanjay: Running smoke matrix now, will paste matrix results here when done. Early result: gcc13 + cuda12 + embedded libstdc++ -> reproducible crash within ~30s. gcc11 + cuda12 -> passes NCCL ring and simple JIT cycles.

maria: Thanks. After rollback let's quarantine the bad image tag and add a blocking check in CI. Also notify support with the incident summary and affected customer list.

devon: Notifying support and owners now. Will follow up with PR link and timeline.

infra-bot: ticket:INC-2026-047 created for tracking; severity:high; assignees: devon,sanjay,maria.

ryan: One more note — GPU firmware mismatch can look similar. Double-check we didn't mix nodes patched with older firmware earlier this week.

sanjay: Checked firmware: all affected nodes show fw 1.4.2, same as unaffected ones. So kernel/driver + embedded libs looks like the vector.

maria: OK. Triage complete for now. Postmortem tasking: build pipeline changes (devon), CI preflight + metric (ryan), cost estimation (alex).

devon: Thanks all. Will push a canary with fixes to one eu-west node group in ~2h.

alex: :thumbsup: Keep the channel updated and flag me if we need to expand to other regions.
